item.text: {"summary":"Fix negative printf width alignment and dynamic precision clamping.","explanation":"The current printf tests show two independent defects. For `test_sprintf(\"%*d\", -5, 42)` and `test_sprintf(\"%2$*1$d\", -5, 42)`, the expected `\"42   \"` is observed as `\"   42\"`: `printf_width_handler` detects a negative width but sets right alignment. For dynamic precision, the boundary assertions expect `fmt::sprintf(\"%.*s\", 0, \"abcdef\")` and `fmt::sprintf(\"%.*s\", -3, \"abcdef\")` to produce `\"\"`, but both produce `\"a\"`; they expect `fmt::sprintf(\"%.*f\", 0, 1.25)` and `fmt::sprintf(\"%.*f\", -3, 1.25)` to produce `\"1\"`, but both produce `\"1.2\"`. The shared `printf_precision_handler` raises every integral dynamic precision to at least 1, so it must clamp at 0. This also explains `fmt::sprintf(\"%.*f\", -13, 1e21)`: expected `\"1000000000000000000000\"`, observed `\"1000000000000000000000.0\"`.","edits":[{"path":"include/fmt/printf.h","old":"specs_.set_align(align::right);\n      width = 0 - width;","new":"specs_.set_align(align::left);\n      width = 0 - width;"},{"path":"include/fmt/printf.h","old":"return max_of(static_cast<int>(value), 1);","new":"return max_of(static_cast<int>(value), 0);"}]}
